title: Negative coverage of the incumbent by media freedom, monthly
author: Erik Wibbels
artifact_handling: Original attachment bytes preserved. No redraw, cropping, recoding, or values reconstructed from pixels.
verification_scope: Visual inspection of the author-supplied figure and caption; numerical reproduction not available.

caption_verified.unit_description: Country-month negative article shares, averaged equally across countries within media-freedom groups.
caption_verified.eligibility: Country-months with at least 30 eligible articles
caption_verified.media_freedom_label: Freedom of Expression and Alternative Sources of Information index
caption_verified.grouping: Terciles of the country-mean media-freedom score over 2022–2025; groups fixed per country for January 2022–December 2025.

panels.description: Share of articles reporting actions opposing the incumbent
Share of articles unfavorable to government reputation
Share of articles critical of the government in title/narration

caption_verified.y_axis: Negative share (mean across countries); fractions rather than percentages; ranges differ by panel.

unverified: Which country identity defines a country-month: evaluated-government country or publication country.
Whether source origin is restricted to the domestic country and whether evaluated government must equal publication country.
Exact 71-country membership and monthly group membership, denominators, zero/uncodable treatment, and handling of missing months.
The author's code, input-file hashes, exact monthly values, and centered-smoothing edge treatment.
Whether the author used the repository's November 4 monthly_polarization_all_countries.csv without additional source filters.

interpretation.claim_supported_by_visible_plot: The ordering of media-freedom groups differs across alignment, reputation and framing.
interpretation.not_established: Domestic-media differences, causal effects of press freedom or regime type, source-selection-adjusted comparisons, or public polarization.
